group_assessment.weighting: A case report of three siblings (one with exome, biochemistry and imaging; two deceased siblings confirmed by targeted testing only) with a homozygous ABAT nonsense variant. GABA values for the index case were obtained retrospectively from stored profiles, in mixed units, and CSF GABA and MRS GABA were not obtained. Genotype-severity correlation is an authors' impression from n = 3 related individuals. No WWOX content.

entries.proposition: The index infant had a homozygous ABAT nonsense variant; both deceased siblings were confirmed homozygous by targeted testing, and exome was not performed on them.
entries.snippet: Whole exome sequencing was not performed for this infant.

entries.proposition: Plasma GABA values are given in mixed units against a reference stated in different units, and a later retrospective serum value differs from both.
entries.snippet: Plasma AA showed GABA at 12 and 15 μmol/L (reference range < 4 nmol/mL) in two samples 3 weeks apart.

entries.proposition: Retrospective analysis of stored profiles gave a serum GABA of 74 nmol/mL and a markedly raised urinary GABA.
entries.snippet: serum GABA levels were increased to 74 nmol/mL (reference range < 4 nmol/mL) and, in the urine, GABA excretion was significantly elevated at 5403 nmol/mg creatinine

entries.proposition: CSF GABA could not be obtained and the MRS GABA peak was not technically possible.
entries.snippet: Lumbar puncture for CSF measures of GABA was attempted thrice without success.

entries.proposition: The first MRI showed cerebellar vermis and hemispheric dysplasia; the day-48 MRI showed new symmetrical restricted diffusion in cortex, subcortical white matter, corpus callosum, internal capsule and corticospinal tracts.
entries.snippet: A follow‐up MRI brain on day 48 revealed new symmetrical and bilateral restricted diffusion within the cortex and subcortical white matter of cerebral hemispheres, and within the corpus callosum, internal capsule and corticospinal tracts.

entries.proposition: The myoclonic jerks in the index infant had no electrographic correlate and were read as non-epileptic myoclonus.
entries.snippet: The myoclonic jerks had no electrographic correlate and were consistent with non‐epileptic myoclonus.

entries.proposition: Flumazenil produced subtle EEG change and a mild gag reflex in an infant with electrocerebral silence; the authors call it unsuccessful in the conclusion.
entries.snippet: A therapeutic trial with flumazenil infusion was attempted but unsuccessful in the index patient.

entries.proposition: The authors suggest a link between a presumed complete loss of function and a more severe phenotype, from this family.
entries.snippet: hints to a possible correlation between presumptive complete loss of function and a more clinically severe phenotype

entries.proposition: Previously reported plasma 2-pyrrolidinone and succinimide may be affected by vigabatrin or topiramate.
entries.snippet: the levels of 2‐pyrrolidinone may be affected by antiseizure medications like vigabatrin or topiramate [10]

entries.proposition: The variant was a VUS at testing and reclassified as likely pathogenic in ClinVar in October 2024.
entries.snippet: This variant was recently reclassified as “Likely Pathogenic” in ClinVar on October 8, 2024.
